modelAnswer: Separating a mixture removes unwanted materials and obtains useful components. It can also help identify properties of known or unknown substances and make useful substances, such as medicines.
stem: Why is it important to separate materials from a mixture?

modelAnswer: A mixture contains two or more substances, such as elements or compounds, that are not chemically combined together. Its components may be present in varying amounts and can be separated by physical methods.

Choose a physical separation method according to the solids' different properties. For example, use magnetic separation if one solid is magnetic, or use sieving when the particles differ in size; the chapter explains that separations exploit differences such as size, shape, mass, density or chemical affinity.
stem: How to separate a mixture of two solids?

modelAnswer: Evaporation separates a dissolved solid from a liquid. The liquid changes into the gaseous phase while the solid is left behind, because liquids vaporize more readily than solids.
Add water to dissolve the sugar, then filter the mixture so sand remains as residue. Evaporate the filtrate to remove water and recover the sugar.
stem: What method will you use to separate a sand and sugar mixture?

modelAnswer: Distillation separates the components of a liquid mixture by heating and cooling. It exploits differences in volatility: vapour is condensed and the collected liquid is called the distillate.

Use fractional distillation. Its fractionating column provides a temperature gradient, allowing alcohol and water to vaporize, cool, condense and be collected separately at their different boiling points.
stem: What technique would you use to separate alcohol from water?

modelAnswer: Separate a mixture of two or more liquids by fractional distillation. The technique separates liquids because each can be vaporized and then condensed at its own boiling point.
stem: How separation of mixtures of two or more liquids is done. Name the separation technique.

modelAnswer: Filtration separates a mixture containing an undissolved solid and a liquid. A filter retains the solid while the liquid passes through, either to isolate the solid or to remove impurities.

Sand and water can be separated by filtration, using filter paper or a muslin cloth as the filter medium. Sedimentation followed by decantation is the other suitable method: let sand settle, then carefully pour off the water.
stem: What technique would you use to separate sand from water? There are two possibilities. Mention their names.
